chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Mother's Lunch, the Boston boarding house and chicken place
summary: McRae describes living on the top floor above Mother's Lunch, where Artie Shaw's men came to eat chicken and play records.

blocks.x: You mentioned Mother's

Lunch. And that was a --
Describe that.
Mother's Lunch was like -- Columbus Avenue and Boston, the colored neighborhood, you know.
That's about five blocks from the Boston Pop, you know. (Inaudible). Like a corner -- five story brownstone house on the corner.
And she used the bottom part, the street level and turned it into a restaurant. Like she had -- sell fried chicken.
She had served dinners and (hey inaudible) famous fried chicken. And she served like dinners and other things like that.
And upstairs, she lived on the second floor. And somebody else lived on the floor -- but I lived on the fourth floor.
I had the whole entire floor, because the grease used to come up from the chicken place -- you know, from the kitchen and get all into --
I moved on the top floor so I could be further away from all that grease and all that --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
This is where we can get up there and make all the noise and wouldn't be disturbing nobody, you know.
And so, like, all the musicians would hang out with me like Tony Pastor and all these different guys would come over from Artie Shaw's band.
That's where we would hang out together, you know, at nighttime. Because we wanted to stay up and get away from Astie (inaudible).
They didn't want nobody to find out what they were doing, so they come over to Mother's Lunch with me, go up on the top floor, have chicken, talk and play records, you know, and things like that.
But this was a famous place for all the musicians, you know. Most of them (inaudible) stayed there, stay in Boston. You go to eat there.
Who didn't stay there, they go to eat at Mother's Lunch that (inaudible) the chicken, because Estelle's Place is up further.
It was a famous chicken place up there.
